<xpln lang="en"><etym lang="tbd">[katz, Teuton. <term lang="fr">chat,</term> Fr.]</etym> A domestick animal that
catches mice, commonly reckoned by naturalists the lowest or­
der of the leonine species.
<term lang="quo">'Twas you incens'd the rabble:
Cats, that can judge as fitly of his worth,
As I can of those mysteries, which heav'n
Will not have earth to know. Shakesp. Coriolanus.</term>
<term lang="quo">Thrice the brinded cat hath mew'd. Shakesp. Macbeth.</term>
<term lang="quo">A cat, as she beholds the light, draws the ball of her eye
small and long, being covered over with a green skin, and di­
lates it at pleasure. Peacham on Drawing.</term></xpln>
